Author: Subhash Chandra Sharma

High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 13354 of 2022
Applicant :- Ravi Kant
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Another
Counsel for Applicant :- Santosh Kumar Shukla

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Ajay Kumar Sharma,Anand Pati Tiwari,Atul Sharma,Rajes
Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Short rejoinder affidavit filed by learned counsel for the applicant is taken on record.

Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
This anticipatory bail application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 372 of 2019 under section 376, 420 I.P.C., Police Station Dibiyapur, District Auraiya.
It is submitted that in this case after investigation charge sheet was filed before the learned court in the year 2019 and prior to submission of charge sheet applicant was granted anticipatory bail during investigation.

After submission of charge sheet which was challenged before this Court under Ravi Kant vs State Of U.P. And Another on 18 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46370692/
1 Section 482 Cr.P.C. which was dismissed as not pressed and direction for appearing the applicant before the learned court was made with observation to the learned court to decide the bail application in the light of law down Satender Kumar Antil's case, in the mean time N.B.W. was issued against the applicant which he challenged before this Court which was dismissed again with the direction to the applicant to appear and move bail application before the learned court within a period of three weeks and move bail application which was to be decided in the light of Satender Kumar Antil's case and this order was passed on 04.11.2022.

entities.text: Ravi Kant vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that applicant was in service in Railway department that was the reason he could not appear before the learned court to move anticipatory bail application which was rejected by the learned court against which present anticipatory bail application was moved by this Court in which interim order was granted in his favour keeping the application pending.
It is further submitted that applicant is ready to face the trial, therefore requested for anticipatory bail.

Learned counsel for the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid and urged that in this case applicant has misused the liberty granted to him during investigation and did not appear before the learned court even after issuance of process though fact of charge sheet was in his knowledge which was challenged by him before this Court and direction was made to appear before the learned trial court and move bail application to be decided in view of law as laid down in Satender Kumar Antil's case.

Even though he did not appear before the learned court and due to none appearance of the applicant N.B.W. was issued against him which was also challenged by the applicant before this Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. which was also dismissed with observation to appear and move bail application before the learned court as aforesaid even though he did not appear before the learned court as a result, process under Section 82 was also issued even though he did not appear ultimately process under Section 83 Cr.P.C. was also issued by the learned court, in this way applicant is continuously avoiding the process of the court and is not co-operating with the trial.

Learned counsel for the opposite party relied his argument on the basis of case decided by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Prem Shankar Prasad Vs. State of Bihar 2021 Supreme (SC) 617 that no anticipatory bail can be granted in favour of an accused against whom proceedings under Sections 82, 83 Cr.P.C. have been initiated.

entities.text: Prem Shankar Prasad Vs. State of Bihar 2021 Supreme (SC) 617
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for both the parties as well as learned A.G.A. and perusal of record, there appears no ground to grant anticipatory bail in favour of the applicant.
Accordingly, this anticipatory bail application is rejected.

However, as per submissions made by learned counsel for the applicant, in case, he appears and moves bail application before the learned Court concerned within a period of 30 days from today, it shall be heard and disposed of as expeditiously as possible in accordance with law as laid down in Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another LL 2022 SC 577 decided on 11.07.2022.
